rows.description: My friend joined a group I find worrying, and I want to rescue him. Wise: keep contact, ask open questions, avoid mocking, and share information gently. Harmful: pressure or secret plots that prove the group right.

rows.description: I fear that the other side's victory will destroy what I value. The fear is sincere. Wise: check facts from varied sources, notice when fear is being sold to me, and act through voting and local work. Harmful: seeing all opponents as enemies.

rows.description: A relative at a family dinner shouts that my views are "brainwashed". I feel insulted and want to retaliate. Wise: decline to debate while heated, say it calmly, and change the subject. Harmful: escalating until dinner is ruined.

rows.description: I love my grandfather but disagree with his politics. Wise: ask what experiences shaped his views, share mine without trying to win, and treasure the person more than the position. Harmful: silent contempt behind polite words.

rows.description: I unfriended everyone who disagrees and feel relieved, then oddly isolated. Wise: boundaries against abuse are fine, but an echo chamber shrinks my mind. Keep some respectful dissent in my life.

rows.description: I admire a political leader and feel proud when he speaks. Wise: support policies on evidence, and stay able to criticise my own side. Harmful: treating criticism of the leader as an attack on me.

rows.description: A viral clip edited to enrage me appears in my feed. I feel a jolt of fury. Wise: pause, search for the full context, and do not share until checked. Harmful: becoming a spreader of outrage.

rows.description: I give time, energy and hope to a cause I believe in, and it gives my life direction. Wise: keep sleep, studies and relationships intact so the commitment lasts. Harmful: burning out or seeing all non-members as enemies.

rows.description: The group is like family, and I hesitate to speak when it makes a bad tactical or ethical choice. Wise: dissent within a movement is loyalty too; say it early and kindly. Harmful: silence that leads to harm.
